title: BECE English Studies: Reading Comprehension - English Studies - Comprehension - Critical Reading (Fact vs. Opinion)
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 1)*

Which of the following statements extracted from the text represents an **opinion** rather than a concrete fact?
options: Over two hundred trees had been planted by the end of the day.
Our village is the most beautiful in the state.
Dig a hole twice as wide as the root ball of the sapling.
Ade managed to plant five mahogany saplings before noon.
questions.explain: Critical reading involves separating fact from a writer's or speaker's deductions. 'Our village is the most beautiful in the state' is a subjective judgment (an opinion) made by Chief Okon. The other options are verifiable facts or specific step-by-step instructions.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 11)*

Which of the following statements extracted from the text represents an **opinion** rather than a verifiable, concrete fact?
options: The 1976 maiden voyage of the Hōkūleʻa went from Hawaii to Tahiti.
The Polynesian settlement of the Pacific is the greatest feat of maritime exploration in human history.
At dusk, the navigator would align the twin hulls of the canoe with a specific rising star.
White terns (manu o Kū) roost on land at night.
questions.explain: Critical reading involves distinguishing between objective data and subjective evaluation. Options a, c, and d state historical or biological facts. Option b is Dr. Silas Vance's subjective assertion/deduction ('the greatest feat'), which is an opinion, regardless of how expert he is.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 21)*

Which of the following statements extracted from the passage represents a subjective **opinion** rather than a concrete historical or scientific fact?
options: The Nok culture flourished in central Nigeria between 1500 BC and 200 AD.
The systematic destruction of these sites by illicit diggers is an absolute tragedy.
Archaeologists scrape away the earth in 10-centimeter layers.
European historians of the early 20th century initially viewed African societies as technologically bereft.
questions.explain: Evaluating an event as an 'absolute tragedy' is a value judgment (an opinion) based on the author's moral or cultural perspective. The other options are verifiable historical facts, methodological steps, or documented historical viewpoints.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 31)*

Which of the following sentences drawn from the passage is an **opinion** rather than a factual statement?
options: The terraced farms of Achi are the most perfectly balanced micro-ecosystems in the world.
Farmers construct a sturdy retaining wall out of locally sourced stone.
Many young people in Achi are migrating to sprawling urban cities.
Small irrigation channels are dug at the back edge of each step.
questions.explain: While stated by a scientist, describing the farms as 'the most perfectly balanced in the world' is a subjective judgment or deduction (an opinion), not an objectively measurable, undeniable fact.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
*(Refer to the comprehension passage in Question 41)*

Which of the following statements extracted from the text represents a subjective **opinion** rather than an objective fact?
options: The *Tubali* system is nothing less than a masterclass in sustainable thermodynamics.
Artisans hand-mold pear-shaped, sun-dried mud bricks, stacking them in circular courses.
A robust foundation of laterite stone is laid to deter rising damp.
Earthen walls have a high thermal mass which absorbs daytime heat and releases it at night.
questions.explain: Evaluating the architectural system as a 'masterclass' is a powerful subjective assertion made by the author (an opinion), whereas options b, c, and d describe verifiable architectural methods and physical thermodynamic properties of earthen walls.
questions.subject: English Studies
